title: Volume 11 · UAT, Cut-Over and Go-Live
subtitle: Lessons 5–8: a UAT script the client signs, a cut-over weekend with a checklist, hypercare that measures itself, and a handover that outlives the consultant
outcomes: Write and run a UAT script whose pass criteria are numbers, not opinions
Plan a cut-over with a dependency order and a rollback position
Run go-live week with a daily hypercare rhythm
Hand over documentation, ownership and a support cadence

slides.title: Write a UAT script the client will sign
bullets: Every test case states the action, the expected number and the evidence
Test by role, because a salesperson and an accountant see different screens
Include the nasty cases: partial delivery, credit limit, return and discounted order
Sign-off per module, with a named business owner, not one signature for everything

rows: Case 1: quote to invoice for 5 blenders
Partial delivery, discount, return, credit limit
Real data, not the demo data
Module signed by the business owner

slides.notes: A UAT case without a number is an opinion, and opinions do not survive a steering committee. Case one in our sample is five blenders at two hundred forty plus ten per cent tax, total one thousand three hundred twenty, cost six hundred, gross profit six hundred. When the tester sees those four figures, the case passes; when they do not, the defect is specific enough to fix.

slides.title: Pass criteria that a steering committee accepts
bullets: Every case passes on expected figures, not on the absence of an error message
Severity one and two defects must be closed, with three and four scheduled
Each module signs separately so one weak area does not block the rest
The signed sheet is the client's acceptance of the system, and your protection

rows: defect fix confirmed by the tester

slides.notes: The figure that matters at the steering committee is zero open severity one defects, not ninety per cent of cases passed. Be explicit about what is deferred, with a date and an owner, because deferred items without owners become the first month's support tickets. A signed sheet with a short deferral list is a better outcome than a verbal yes.

slides.title: Plan the weekend in dependency order
bullets: Cut-over is a sequence, and each step unblocks the next one
Freeze the old system before extracting balances, or the numbers will move
Have a rollback position: the old system stays readable for one month
One person owns the clock and one person owns the checklist, never the same person

rows: One sale, one purchase, one payment
Users know where to log in

slides.notes: The cut-over plan fits on one page and that is the test of it. If a step has no owner or no evidence, it will be skipped at two in the morning. Keep the old system readable for a month and say so in writing, because that rollback position is what allows the client to say yes on Friday rather than postpone a week.

slides.title: Hypercare with numbers, then hand over
bullets: Hypercare is a fortnight of daily rhythm: tickets, blockers, and a single decision channel
Measure the same five things daily so the trend is visible, not the anecdote
Hand over documentation, owners and a support cadence, or you become the support desk
The exit criterion is agreed before go-live, not negotiated at the end

rows: invoices, stock errors, ticket count, close progress, user logins
Runbook, config worksheet, UAT sheet, access review

slides.notes: Five metrics, fifteen minutes, every morning for a fortnight: that is hypercare, and it ends on a date the client agreed before go-live. The handover pack is the same documentation produced during the project, which is why it must be written as you go rather than reconstructed. A consultant who leaves a runbook and a calendar invite is the one who gets the phase two call.

slides.title: Evidence for each cut-over step
bullets: Every step leaves a document, and the documents are what the auditor reads
The freeze note, the count sheet and the opening trial balance are the core three
A smoke test that posts correctly is the last gate before users are let in
Rollback stays available for a month, and saying so reduces go-live anxiety

rows: one sale, one purchase, one payment posted

slides.notes: Cut-over is judged on documents rather than on a feeling that it went well. Lay the five items on the table at the Sunday evening review, and either they exist or they do not. If the smoke test posted incorrectly, that is the moment to use the rollback position, not Monday morning when users are already entering data.

slides.title: The numbers that end the fortnight
bullets: Ticket count, invoice count, stock errors, close progress and logins are the five daily measures
A falling ticket count with a rising invoice count means the client is taking over
Open severity one at zero for three consecutive days is the usual exit signal
The exit review is a meeting, not an opinion, and it produces a signed note

rows: signed with an agreed support cadence

slides.notes: Five numbers on one line each day, and the trend does the talking. When tickets fall while invoices rise, the client has absorbed the system, and the exit meeting is a formality rather than a risk. If stock errors are flat rather than falling, the warehouse process is still wrong, and staying another week is cheaper than a year of corrections.

slides.title: Go or no-go, decided on evidence
bullets: Each criterion has a number, so the meeting is short and the decision is defensible
Any single red row is a no-go unless the client formally accepts the risk
The acceptance must be written, dated and signed by the project sponsor
A delayed go-live is cheaper than an uncontrolled one, in cost and in reputation

rows: every user attended or was covered

slides.notes: Put this table on the screen in the go/no-go meeting and work down it row by row; the decision takes fifteen minutes and nobody can claim afterwards that they were not consulted. Green everywhere is a go. One red row is a conversation about risk, documented in the minutes with a name against it.

slides.title: The handover pack that ends the engagement
bullets: The pack is the project's memory, and it must be usable without the consultant
Configuration worksheet, opening balances, UAT results and runbook are the core four
Named owners for each cadence, or the pack becomes shelfware
A short training session on the pack itself is what makes it live

rows: Proof the business accepted the system

slides.notes: A consultant's reputation is built in the last two weeks, and it is built on how little the client needs to call afterwards. Hand over five documents, name five owners, put five meetings in the calendar, and then step back. The work is finished when the client runs the rhythm without you, not when the invoices are issued.

lab.title: Lab · Run UAT, cut over and open the hypercare log
steps: Write five UAT cases with exact expected figures for sales, purchase, stock and accounts
Assign each case to a named business owner and record the tester
Execute the cases in a test company and log any defect with severity
Confirm zero open severity one defects before sign-off
Produce the one-page cut-over plan with owners and evidence
Freeze, extract, load and prove the opening trial balance
Smoke test one sale, one purchase and one payment after go-live
Open the hypercare log and record the five daily metrics
lab.done: Done when all five UAT cases pass on their figures with a signature, the opening balances balance, the smoke tests post correctly, and the hypercare log has an owner and an exit date.

quiz.question: What makes a UAT case pass?
quiz.why: A case passes on numbers: 1,320.00 total, 600.00 cost, 600.00 gross profit. The absence of an error message proves nothing.

quiz.question: Which defect state blocks go-live?
quiz.why: Severity one blocks go-live; lower severities can be scheduled with an owner and a date, recorded at sign-off.

quiz.question: Why keep the old system readable after cut-over?
options: As a rollback position and reference for the first month
quiz.why: A readable old system gives the client a rollback position and a reference while the new balances settle.

quiz.question: What is the exit criterion for hypercare?
options: Open severity one at zero, agreed before go-live
quiz.why: The exit is measured against a criterion agreed before go-live, so it is a decision rather than a negotiation at the end.

quiz.question: Which document proves the business accepted the system?
quiz.why: The signed UAT sheet is the formal acceptance, supported by defect closure and retest evidence.

memory.spine: A script the client signs, a weekend in dependency order, a fortnight measured in numbers, and a pack that outlives the consultant.

device.label: Script, sequence, numbers, hand over
expansion: A test case states the action, the expected number and the evidence, and the client signs it
Pass means the expected figure appears, not that no error message was shown
Cut over in dependency order, because each step unblocks the next one
Hypercare is a fortnight of daily numbers: tickets, invoices, stock errors, close progress and logins
The handover pack must be usable without the consultant in the room

cards.q: What makes a UAT case pass?
cards.a: The expected figure appears on screen, not merely that the screen did not produce an error.

cards.q: Why is cut over ordered rather than parallel?
cards.a: Each step produces the input for the next, so reordering it creates work that must be redone.

cards.q: Which five numbers are measured daily in hypercare?
cards.a: Tickets raised, invoices posted, stock errors, close progress and logins.
A go or no go decision on evidence where every criterion carries a number and someone signs it.

cards.q: What goes into the handover pack?
cards.a: Configuration record, mapping workbook, UAT sign off, cut over log, open items and how to run the close.

trap.what: UAT is signed off because no errors were raised during the session.
trap.why: Nobody compared figures, so the first month end discovers the wrong tax template and the sign off protects the vendor, not the client.

narration: The last two weeks decide how the project is remembered. UAT is not a demo: every case states an action and an expected number, five blenders at two hundred forty plus tax is one thousand three hundred twenty, cost six hundred, gross profit six hundred, and the case passes only when those figures appear. Go or no-go is decided on five rows of evidence, with a written acceptance for anything red. Cut-over is a one-page sequence with owners, and the old system stays readable as a rollback position. Then hypercare: five metrics, fifteen minutes, every morning, ending on the date agreed before go-live. Hand over the runbook, the worksheet, the opening pack and the access review, and step back. The measure of a finished engagement is not the invoice, it is a client running their own close, their own UAT for the next change, and their own access review without calling you, because the rhythm lives in their calendar rather than in your notes.
